tasks.spec:
You are a code and story-data worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of freytag-forge; edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. You own the story data (data/stories/continuity-initiative/*), the NEW file tests/test_guard_vocabulary.py, EVERY existing test, fixture and checked-in generated artifact that encodes the old vocabulary behavior (tests/, tests/fixtures, .plans/disclosure-matrix.md and .json, .plans/disclosure-decisions.md with one dated note, item/affordance payload fixtures), and docs/ only if a doc states the old behavior. Do NOT edit storygame/ code, bench/, frontend/ or scripts/. Never run anything billed or networked. KEEP IT SIMPLE: smallest data edits that work; add no new rules to code.

LEAVE THE REPO CONSISTENT, NOT PATCHED. Your change deliberately alters behavior, so existing expectations of the OLD behavior must be updated in the same change: a test that asserted 'infrastructure corridor' (singular) is guarded, a payload fixture lacking the new house_gate/facility_gate things, the affordance matrix, the checked-in disclosure matrix. Regenerate generated artifacts with their generator (for the disclosure matrix run scripts/disclosure_matrix.py as tests/test_disclosure_matrix.py shows; for others find the generator the failing test names). Update a hand-written expectation only when it encodes exactly the behavior you are deliberately changing, edit it to the new correct value, and never delete a test or loosen an unrelated assertion. In your final message list every pre-existing test or artifact you changed and the one-line reason. Never leave a failing test with the note that it is out of scope; the full suite must be green.

A previous attempt left a partial change at /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/stage5-notes/guard-vocab-partial.patch (read it; start from it only if it is correct, it failed 11 tests at the time). Currently failing tests it left: tests/test_disclosure_matrix.py::test_matrix_is_deterministic_and_fresh, tests/test_late_scene_repro.py corridor tests for 2A and 3B, and others in the item payload and affordance matrix suites.

READ FIRST: docs/world-model-grounding.md (Things, Names), docs/markdown-story-authoring.md (field syntax), docs/narrator-writing-guide.md if you write any narrator-facing text, .plans/disclosure-decisions.md, and storygame/runtime/narration_safety.py::_validate_segments (how a term is accepted or refused: entity alias check, known_terms/leak terms, protected terms, disclosure guards). `scripts/disclosure_matrix.py` shows how to probe the real validator offline with a scripted segment; reuse its approach in your tests.

OWNER RULE (Brandon, 2026-10-17): 'If an item is visible in the scene it can be referred to.' Public ordinary words must not be refused in their own scene; secrets stay secret; a term must stay refused in scenes where the thing is not present. The decision table says: 'park bench' is Public (the secret is WHICH bench Michelle used and what she left), 'infrastructure corridor' is Public as a place (knowing it exists gives no access; access is earned in 2A.3 via k_sl_2a_c_r2), and the 1A house gate is an ordinary visible thing.

THE FOUR PROBLEMS (verify each by probe BEFORE editing; a probe is a scripted narration segment through NarrationSafetyValidator on a state for that scene with the earning knowledge NOT yet earned):
 1. 'front gate' / 'house gate' in 1A. The patrol marks the house's front gate with reflective tape (plot.md 1A, ~lines 156-160; knowledge k_sl_1a_f_r2, must_convey 'front gate'). It is only a reveal phrase, not a declared thing, so it is refused before the tape is found. FIX: declare a fixed item `house_gate` (name 'house gate', scoped_aliases [front gate, gate]) in world.yaml, add it to scene 1A item_ids with an item_placements entry (parent outside_house or mcgehee_home, whichever resolves; check that 1A's other placements and the grounding guide's tree rules are satisfied). Do not change k_sl_1a_f_r2 delivery text unless a probe proves it needed.
 2. 'front gate' in 2A (the facility's gate; series B hosted run refused 'narration mentions unavailable entity/knowledge front gate' at turn 30). The word belongs to 1A's house gate, so in 2A the narrator should name the facility entrance. FIX: declare a fixed item `facility_gate` (name 'facility gate', scoped_aliases [gate, front gate]) placed in the 2A facility area and in 2A item_ids, so 2A narration may say 'gate' or 'front gate' for it while 1A's `house_gate` is out of scope there. If two scoped aliases collide in one scene, rename in the fiction rather than loosening checks. Check plot.md 2A for any prose that already calls the entrance something else and keep that wording.
 3. 'park bench' in 1A. It is a must_convey phrase of k_sl_1a_b_r1 (the card's contents) and an entity name in 1B, so it is refused in 1A before the card is read. The table says it is public. FIX: give k_sl_1a_b_r1 an explicit `leak_terms` list that keeps its genuinely secret phrases (copy the current multi-word aliases/must_convey phrases that should stay guarded: dead drop, exchange point, the card's recording and files phrases) and omits 'park bench' and 'bench in the park'. Per the grounding guide, with `leak_terms` present only the listed multi-word phrases are blocked. Also confirm the declared 1B item `park_bench` does not make the word 'park bench' unavailable in 1A through the entity-alias check; if it does, the smallest fix is a public mention allowance you can express in data (for example listing 'park bench' as a scoped alias on a 1A-visible thing is NOT acceptable, since no bench is in the 1A scene). If data cannot fix it without a code change, STOP on this item, leave it unfixed, and explain exactly which line of narration_safety.py refuses it.
 4. Singular 'infrastructure corridor' in 2A and 3B. It is an alias of the reveal k_sl_2a_c_r2 (aliases list, leak_terms entry) while the plural place name `infrastructure_corridors` already passes. The table says it is public as a place. FIX: in knowledge.yaml remove the singular phrase from that reveal's guarded vocabulary (aliases and leak_terms) so it is not guarded, but keep it in action_evidence and must_convey so the reveal still requires the player to enter it; the singular form is already an alias of the declared `infrastructure_corridors` location in world.yaml, so it stays nameable. The reveal must not be earned by merely naming the corridor.
Do NOT touch bare 'card' (handled elsewhere).

TESTS in tests/test_guard_vocabulary.py (offline, hermetic): for each fixed term, a scripted-segment probe through the real validator showing: accepted in its own scene before the earning knowledge; still refused in at least one earlier or unrelated scene where the thing is not present (for 'front gate' in 1A vs 2A: 'house gate' refused in 2A and facility gate fine in 2A; 'park bench' accepted in 1A and the secret phrase 'dead drop' still refused in 1A before the card is read; 'infrastructure corridor' accepted in 2A and 3B, while earning k_sl_2a_c_r2 still requires the enter-corridor command evidence). Add a test that every existing disclosure/never-released secret in .plans/disclosure-decisions.md ('JANUS', 'Phase Two', 'purge clock', 'memory card') is still refused where it was. Run tests/test_disclosure_matrix.py and the authoring-quality tests; if the checked-in .plans/disclosure-matrix.md/json is compared by a test and now legitimately differs, report it in your final message rather than editing files you do not own.

PACKAGE-PAYLOAD CAPTURE DIFF (required by the project): run the shipped narrator payload capture `.plans/world-model-s1/prompt_capture.py` (read its header for usage; network must stay stubbed) on the base commit and on your change, diff the outputs, and paste the diff summary in your final message. The only expected differences are the new THINGS lines for house_gate in 1A and facility_gate in 2A.

HOW TO RUN. Confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c \"import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)\"` prints a path inside this worktree. Iterate with `PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --no-cov -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_guard_vocabulary.py tests/test_disclosure_matrix.py tests/test_disclosure_guards.py`, then the whole tests directory (use -m authoring_quality too), then ruff check and ruff format --check (line length 120) via /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/ruff on your .py file.

COMPLETION RULE: do not stop until the full suite is green and ruff is clean, or an item is explicitly left unfixed with the exact refusing code line named. Finish by listing files changed, pasting the pytest summary, the per-term before/after probe results, the capture diff summary, and any items left unfixed.
